title: EV Charging Solutions by Operating Context | Anari Energy
meta: Four charging solutions organised by the constraint that decides the design: public corridors, fleet depots, PV plus storage, and destination sites.

sections.h1: The site decides the design, not the product catalogue.
sections.lede: A corridor site, a bus depot and a hotel car park fail for different reasons. Each solution below starts from the constraint that will actually bind your project — grid capacity, dwell time, duty cycle or climate.
sections.credit: Bus depot, Czechia — twelve DC units under canopy

sections.lede: Pick the row that matches how the site will actually be used. Everything downstream — power, storage, connectors, maintenance model — follows from it.

items.title: Commercial & public charging
items.text: Corridor and urban sites where the grid connection, not the charger, sets the timeline.

items.title: Fleet & depot charging
items.text: Overnight windows and duty cycles: the site must survive the worst night of the year.

items.title: PV, storage & off-grid
items.text: When the grid cannot deliver the power on time, storing it first changes what is buildable.

sections.h2: Four questions before any equipment is chosen
sections.lede: Every solution page answers these in the same order, so the comparison between two sites is a comparison of constraints, not of marketing copy.

items.title: Power available
items.text: The kVA the site can actually draw, and what the utility will approve.

items.title: Dwell & duty
items.text: How long vehicles stay, and how many sessions the site must serve at peak.

items.title: Climate envelope
items.text: Ambient heat, monsoon, dust or cold — which component derates first.

items.title: Operating model
items.text: Who runs it, who fixes it, and what happens on the worst night.

sections.h2: Solutions are only real if they shipped
sections.lede: The cases below were selected for the same reason the solutions pages exist: each one had a binding constraint that decided the design.
